findings.summary: All three figure captions (lines 19-21) omit the terminal residual and the converged flag, and every one of the three states drawn is a non-converged terminal state (MAST-U 45272 misfit 50, TCV workshop 6.978, ITER 135013 10.03; converged=no on all three per the table above the panels). The panels draw tidy closed contours and the legend asserts a two-state comparison, so a reader sees what looks like a solved equilibrium and has no way to learn from the figure that the fit was still moving when its 96-pass budget ended. The section's plotting rule asks for the terminal residual and the converged flag in the caption; the captions carry neither, and instead repeat the encoding the legend already gives. Folded: add the residual and converged flag to each caption in a follow-up fragment edit.

The legend names only the two contour families (grey imas-efit, blue nova) and gives no entry for the triangle and cross marks, and the captions say only 'both null sets' without saying what the marks are. A reader is therefore shown a solid triangle at the core and cross marks near the divertor in two shades with no statement anywhere on the figure or in its caption that the triangle is the magnetic axis and the cross the admitted X-point, nor which shade belongs to which state. On the ITER and MAST-U panels, where the two shades coincide, the marks are the only place the null comparison can be read, so the missing vocabulary costs the reader the one comparison the markers exist to make. Folded: add one clause naming the marker vocabulary (and stating the marker sizes differ between the two states) to each caption.

_panel builds one 14.0 x 7.2 in canvas (aspect 1.94:1) and lets the single subplot fill its width while poloidal_axes holds an equal aspect, so each machine is drawn at its own tall aspect inside a wide canvas. Measured on the delivered PNGs, the plotted content occupies x 557-841 (MAST-U), x 557-838 (TCV) and x 557-838 (ITER) of a 1399 px width: about 20 % of the canvas. Roughly 80 % of the figure's width is empty white, and the contour detail and the null markers are drawn at a fifth of the size the canvas could give them. That is why the grey reference, legible at full resolution, degrades to a faint halo at the page column width used by the evidence page. Folded: either size the canvas width to each machine's aspect, or place the three panels side by side on one shared-scale canvas.

In the TCV panel the reference and nova contours nearly coincide, so the 2.6 pt grey line is almost entirely covered by the 1.4 pt blue line drawn over it. At full resolution the grey is still visible as a wide band with the blue running inside it, but at the page column width the reference disappears and the panel reads as a single blue contour set, which is the one reading the panel exists to prevent. Exempted: the encoding is the documented design (a wide reference beneath a narrow subject, so agreement reads as a narrow line centred in a wide one), and the vector SVG served to the page preserves the 2.6 pt grey where a raster downsampling loses it; the finding is recorded so a future caption or layout change can address the page-scale read.

In the ITER panel the lower-left flux region is drawn as a fan of blue and grey contours that terminates against the bottom-left wall corner, and several arcs stop short in the interior, with nothing on the figure or in its caption saying what that region is. Measured, the content bounding box stops at y 672 of 719, so this is not a canvas clip: the contours end where the underlying node grid meets the wall. A reader cannot tell from the panel whether this is a legitimate private-flux or scrape-off region truncated by the grid or a solved structure that the wall cut off. Exempted: the truncation is a faithful rendering of the data boundary the fit was solved over, and the panel shows it as it is rather than hiding it; a caption clause naming the region would remove the ambiguity.

In the ITER panel the two null-marker pairs overlap almost entirely: at the X-point the blue cross sits on the grey cross at about (646, 550) with only a sliver of grey showing beneath, and at the axis the blue triangle covers the grey one. At full resolution a careful reader can see both shades; at the page column width each pair reads as a single dark mark, so the figure silently loses the statement that the two states agree on the null locations rather than that only one state has nulls. The same overlap is present but milder on MAST-U at about (631, 600). Exempted: the overlap records a genuine coincidence of the two null estimates and both marks are distinguishable at native resolution on the delivered PNG.
